question: The period between two FIFA Football World Cups is _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**4 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The FIFA World Cup is held every four years, making it one of the most anticipated events in the football calendar.
 
• The tournament brings together the top national teams from around the world to compete for the prestigious title.
 
• The four-year cycle allows teams time to develop and qualify through regional tournaments and qualifiers.
 
• Historically, the FIFA World Cup has been held every four years since its inception in 1930, with exceptions during World War II.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association)**

 
 
• FIFA is the international governing body of association football, futsal, and beach soccer, established in 1904.
 
• Its headquarters are in Zurich, Switzerland.
 
• FIFA is responsible for organizing major international football tournaments, including the FIFA World Cup.
 
 
 
• **FIFA World Cup**
 
 
• The FIFA World Cup is the most prestigious football tournament in the world, first held in 1930.
 
• It features 32 teams competing over a month-long period.
 
• The tournament is watched by millions of people worldwide, making it one of the biggest sporting events.
 
• The reigning champions are the French national football team, who won the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia.
 
 
 
• **Qualification Process**
 
 
• National teams must go through a qualification process to earn a spot in the World Cup.
 
• Each of the six FIFA continental zones has its own qualifying tournaments.
 
• The qualification process typically takes place over the three years leading up to the World Cup.
